Might be: "Even if your purity makes you seem corrupted, keep company with the wicked"? Hmm. Let's parse: "گر چه پاکی تو را پلید کند" = "Although your purity may make you (appear) impure"? Actually "پلید" means vile, corrupt. So "Even though your purity makes you vile"? That seems contradictory. Perhaps meaning: "If your purity makes you seem vile, sit with the wicked"? The second line: "با بدان کم نشین که صحبت بد". Means "Sit less with the wicked, for bad company." So overall: Advice to avoid bad company. So theme: warning against associating with wicked people.

Option 2: "خرمن عقل و عافیت سوزد - حسد آنجا که افروزد". Means "The granary of intellect and health burns - envy where it ignites." So perhaps talking about envy causing destruction of intellect and health. Theme: Envy is destructive.

Option 3: "چون عاقبت کار چنین خواهد بود - گر ما می و معشوق گزیدیم چه باک". Means "When the outcome of affairs will be like this - even if we choose wine and beloved, what fear?" So perhaps acceptance of fate; indifferent to choices, fatalism. Theme: Accepting destiny, carefree.

Option 4: "خیــــانــــت روا داردم در حـــــرم - که چون بدگهر پرورم الجرم". Means "I committed treason in the sanctuary, because as a bad-tempered (or evil) nurturer, the crime." Hard to parse.
